sentences.text:
Mr. Balmoori Venugopal Rao vs The Union Of India on 10 July,
2025
 Honourable Sri Justice N.V.Shravan Kumar
 Writ Petition No.19763 of 2025
Order:

entities.text: Balmoori Venugopal Rao vs The Union Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.Gadi Praveen Kumar, Deputy Solicitor General of India appearing for respondent Nos.1 and 5, Sri.M.Ramu, learned standing counsel for NHAI appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3 and Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent No.4.
With their consent this writ petition is taken up for disposal at the stage of admission itself.

2. This Writ petition is filed seeking the following prayer:-
"to declare the impugned Memo in R.C No.C2/16/2016 dated 13.09.2024 issued by the fifth respondent as being arbitrary, illegal, in violation of the procedure contemplated under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 R/w. Section 3G (5) of the National Highway Act, 1956 and set aside the same and consequently direct the fifth respondent to initiate the arbitral proceedings by taking the claim petition on record and proceed with the same in accordance with the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996."

3. Brief facts stated in this writ Petition are that the petitioners claims to be the owners and possessors of Plots bearing No.1, admeasuring 210 Sq.yards and Plot No.2 admeasuring 403 Sq.yards, in Sy.No.108, situated at Kyathanpally Village, Mandamarri Mandal, Mancherial District.

The case of the petitioners is that pursuant to requisition dated 15.10.2016 made by respondent No.3, petitioners land was acquired for the purpose of laying National Highway No.363 and thereafter respondent No.4, under Section 3A (1) of National Highways Act, 1956, initiated land acquisition proceedings and issued notifications dated 09.08.2017 and 06.03.2019.

Further case of the petitioners is that though acquisition notifications were issued, no individual notices were served on the petitioners for objections and subsequent to notifications, an award was passed by respondent No.4, however, copy of the award was also not served on the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners vide letter dated 19.12.2019, requested respondent No.4 to issue a copy of award.
When the same was not served, the petitioners through Right to Information Act, obtained the copy of award dated 18.10.2019, in the first week of July,2020.

Thereafter, the petitioners came to know that the compensation awarded by the respondent No.4 is not adequate as the true market value prevailing in the subject area was not reflected in the award dated 18.10.2019.

However, in the meantime, Covid-19 pandemic hit the entire country and a lock-down was imposed and since the petitioners were also not given an opportunity of hearing and raising objections, the petitioners addressed a letter dated 08.04.2022 and requested respondent No.3 to appoint an independent arbitrator for the purpose of determining proper compensation and when the same was not considered, petitioners filed W.P.No.38753 of 2022 and this Court vide order dated 26.10.2022 had Mr. Balmoori Venugopal Rao vs The Union Of India on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51061195/

sentences.text:
1 closed the writ petition with the following observations:-
"4.

When the matter came up for consideration, Sri Alladi Ravinder, learned Standing Counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3, brought to the notice of this Court that a Notification was already issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways Bearing No.S.O.1306(E), dated 21.03.2018, and the District Collectors of Mancherial and the Komurambheem Asifabad were appointed as arbitrators for the purpose of Sub-section (5) of Section 3G of the Act, 1956, who shall exercise the powers conferred and perform the duties imposed on them and a copy of the said Notification is also furnished to learned counsel for the petitioners.

entities.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 5. In the circumstances, the grievance of the petitioners, as agitated, does not survive.
The writ petition is accordingly closed granting liberty to the petitioners to approach the District Collectors, who are now appointed as arbitrators under Section 3G (5) of the Act, 1956.
There shall be no order as to costs."

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that pursuant to the order dated 26.10.2022 in W.P.No.38753 of 2022, petitioners under Section 3G (5) of the Act, 1956, filed claim petition before respondent No.5.

Thereafter respondent No.5 vide impugned Memo bearing R.C.No.C2/16/2016 dated 13.09.2024, stated that the claim petition has been filed after lapse of (3) years of period i.e.,
from the date of passing of award to the date of claim of appellants and did not considered the claim petition.

Thereafter, the petitioners on 29.09.2024 issued a notice to respondent No.5 and stated that the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated 10.01.2022 in Suo Motu Writ Petition No.3 of 2020, while considering the then prevailing Covid-19 condition in the entire country had excluded the period between 15.03.2020 and 28.02.2022 for the purpose of limitation as may be prescribed under any general or special law in respect of all judicial or quasi-judicial proceeding and further requested respondent No.5 to withdraw the memo dated 13.09.2024 and fix an early schedule for the arbitration proceeding.

entities.text: Suo Motu Writ Petition No.3 of 2020
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: However, the same is not considered.
Aggrieved by the same, petitioners filed this writ petition.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that at the time of acquisition proceedings, the petitioners were neither given an opportunity of giving objections nor the petitioners were served with a copy of the award 18.10.2019.

The petitioners had obtained the copy of award through RTI Act, in the first week of July, 2020 and in view of the Covid-19 pandemic, the petitioners vide letter dated 08.04.2022 requested for appointment of sole arbitrator and thereafter in pursuant to the order dated 26.10.2022 in W.P.No.38753 of 2022, petitioners under Section 3G (5) of the Act, 1956,
filed claim petition before respondent No.5 on 03.01.2024.

6. The main grievance of the petitioners is that inspite of clarification in notice dated 29.09.2024 with respect to limitation aspect, respondent No.5 had not withdrawn impugned Memo bearing R.C.No.C2/16/2016 dated 13.09.2024 and not scheduled any date for hearing the claim petition,
hence, pray this Court to set aside the impugned memo dated 13.09.2024 and direct the respondent No.5 to commence hearing of petitioners claim petition.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for respondents pray this Court to pass appropriate orders.
8. Heard and perused the material available on record.

Upon perusal of the record, it is noticed that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in suo moto writ petition No.3 of 2020 had dealt with the limitation aspect and vide order dated 10.01.2022 had excluded the period between 15.03.2020 and 28.08.2022 for the purpose of limitation and the same was intimated to respondent No.5 through notice dated 29.09.2024.

Inspite of the same, respondent No.5, while deciding the maintainability of the petitioners claim petition, failed to exclude the period between 15.03.2020 and 28.08.2022,
and issued memo dated 13.09.2024.

Hence, this Court deems it appropriate to set aside the impugned memo dated 13.09.2024.
9.

Having considered the above facts and circumstances and in the light of observation made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in suo moto writ petition No.3 of 2020 dated 10.01.2022, the impugned Memo bearing R.C.No.C2/16/2016 dated 13.09.2024 is set aside and accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of directing the respondent No.5 to initiate the arbitral proceedings and after giving a fair opportunity of hearing to the parties, the respondent No.5 shall pass appropriate orders, strictly in accordance with law.
10.
With the above directions, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
No order as to costs.
